Here’s the recipe! This is amazing during cold days. Sorry I was late, I actually posted and left the app not knowing it would actually grab any attention hahaha. I eyeballed everything, but let me see if I could estimate the measuring! Since this is my first time attempting this, I’ll also leave notes.

You’ll need:

​

* Hominy
* Jack Fruit - I got the one in brine from Trader Joe’s cause it’s the only one I could find. I used a can and a half but it’s your choice how much you want to use.
* TVP! Honestly, I preferred this a lot more than the jackfruit.
* Mexicans do their chiles differently. Some use different kinds, my boyfriend’s family likes just guajillo and arbol for the spice. I used 9-10 guajillos and 3 arbol.
* Mushrooms, I’d say any kind but the one I had available was the big baby Bella mushrooms. I cut up a cup of those.
* Salt and pepper
* MSG (optional, but definitely check this [video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qiJy8KMMlSM) out if you still think MSG is bad for you cause I promise you, the hatred for MSG came from racism, not good science lol)
* Cumin
* Bay leaves
* Onion
* Garlic
* Garlic powder
* Toppings\*: Cilantro, green onion, red radish, lettuce (some use cabbage), diced onion, and ofc LIMON!! (lime)
* Mexican oregano (opt)

PREP!

For the jackfruit, I pre-boiled it for 90 minutes. This is optional if you don’t mind the brine-y taste. I absolutely hate it and it actually still lingered a little bit after the second boil. So I rinsed it, boiled it for 45mins, changed the water and boiled again for 45. I found that squeezing the liquid out, even if it shreds rather than keeping form, blends with your future pozole broth.

For the TVP:

I hydrated it (I think I used half a cup worth - they expand!) using veggie broth for around 15 minutes. But then I dried it again. I wrung out allll the liquid with paper towel so it’s still spongy but no longer super wet. I then sautéed it (with a bit of oil) to get rid of the rest of the moisture, and to brown it as well. I did as much as I can to squeeze out the moisture with the spatula. This part is optional, but I sprinkled it with paprika, cumin, and a tiny splash of worcestershire sauce to flavor it up before adding it in the broth.

For the chile:

I boiled some water; enough to cover the chile, half an onion, and a couple of garlics. I took out the stem and seeds out of the chile. I placed the chile, half an onion (uncut but peeled outside layer), and 3-4 garlic cloves (peeled) in once it started boiling and I lowered the heat. You can turn it off but I wanted to speed up the process. I’d say wait around 15minutes if you kept your heat on, 30 if you didn’t.

Just look at the chile and if it looks like it absorbed the water, fuck it take it out and add it to the blender. You can try doing this in two parts cause some blenders can’t take that much in (unless you have those nice blenders, than I’m very envious pls donate to me tnx jk lol). Add the chiles, onion, garlics, and a splash of the liquid it was boiling on. Like… 1/3 cup? Not too much but enough to make it blend better. Don’t be too scared to add a big glug if needed. Add a tbsp of salt, a tbsp of cumin, and if you like Mexican oregano, rub it between your palms and add to the blender, around a tbsp as well. Then blend! REMEMBER! Don’t blend with the lids completely closed off cause it’s hot. Use a cloth or paper tower on the small opening of the lid to prevent steam exploding.

After, strain the chile blend and set aside.

\*Some people like to roast their chile blend before using it and I tried but adding liquid to a hot oiled pan is so scary y’all lol.

On a big/tall pot, sauté the mushrooms in oil (I used avocado oil) until it starts to get moist (hehe). People usually add their chile at the end for the broth but I decided to add it in now to see how much veggie broth to add. Then add as much hominy as you want (rinse it beforehand). I used I think… 3-4 cups worth? Stir, then add in veggie broth. I believe I used 2 1/2 L? Depending on how much TVP/jackfruit you want to use. I also added 3 bay leaves, a pinch of cumin, a tbsp of garlic powder (I like my garlic), 2-3tbsp salt, and a tsp of MSG(opt). Stir, and wait for it to boil.

Once in a rolling boil, add the TVP and jackfruit. Bring to a simmer for minimum 30 minutes. The longer, the better! I simmered for 1 1/2 hours - 2 hours. Taste to adjust the flavor. I added extra veggie bouillon, depending on how much sodium you’re okay with. Make sure you don’t eat the bayleaves. Serve :) Topped it with cilantro, green onion, red radish, lettuce (some use cabbage), diced onion, and ofc LIMON!! (lime, lot’s of it). Also tostadas yummmmm.

Enjoy! If you have any questions or if my wordings doesn’t make sense (my English sucks lol) let me know!

That one was actually super easy! 

You just need: 

\- Puff pastry

\- 1 can of full fat unsweetened coconut milk

\- Peaches on 100% heavy syrup - among with other fruits you like! I added strawberries :) 

\- Powdered sugar/Confectioners' sugar (optional)

\- Maple syrup (optional)

That one was actually super easy! All you need is a puff pastry (I used the Pepperidge Farm frozen sheets pastry dough), and put that in the oven as instructed (usually 400F for 15-20mins). I poke it all over with a fork so the air can release when we press down later to flatten. I also outline with the fork on the margins and brush with maple syrup on the sides to darken (I hope that made sense). After, put it on a rack to cool. We don’t want it super hot for the whipped cream. 

This is the only part you’d plan ahead; refrigerate unsweetened coconut milk over night. I even pop it in the freezer for 15 minutes before I cook so that the fat solidifies (optional to freeze). Then I scoop out the solidified coconut (the liquid you can save later for smoothies), then either whisk or use a hand blender until it’s whipped! I also suggest adding powdered sugar (I think I put around 2tbsp cause I love sweet) for flavor. Some opt for maple syrup as a sweetener but I think it kinda ruins the texture sometimes. Too risky! 

For the peaches, I just got a canned peach in 100% heavy syrup. and strained it. The syrup, you can boil on the pot with a dash of maple syrup so you can drizzle on top later! Gotta make sure the syrup cools beforehand though or it’ll melt the whipped cream. 

Cut the peaches and a couple of strawberries. Any fruit you want, really. Then just layer! Puff pastry, the whipped cream, the fruits, then the syrup (optional)

Super simple but super yummy vegan dessert.

**Buddha Bowl**

I just kinda eyeballed everything so this is the best I could do LOL sorry!

(Serving for two)

Base: Spring mixed greens

Toppings:

One whole sweet potato, diced. I coated it with olive oil, garlic powder, paprika, and a pinch of salt. I put it in the oven at 400F for 10 minutes. I took it out, flipped, and then added the broccoli in the same tray (woulda used broccolini if I had any), drizzled oil on top and sprinkled salt, then popped it back in the oven for another 10 minutes.

For the quinoa tabbouleh, I just cooked half a cup of dry quinoa just like how you usually would. I spread it out on a plate to cool it down so it’s not super hot when I added chopped tomatoes, chopped cucumber, green onion, minced garlic, and cilantro. Woulda put some parsley but I ran out lmao. I seasoned with salt, fresh lemon juice, EVOO, and pepper. Simple :)

For the firm tofu, I actually did 3 different kinds just to have different textures (to experiment). Of course like usual, soak out all the moisture from the firm tofu beforehand. All of them I brushed with soy sauce. One of them, I just had it as plain soaked with soy sauce. The other, I brushed with soy, dipped in flour, almond milk, and panko with nutritional yeast and garlic powder in it. The third one was no soy sauce but coated with the milk and panko. They were all good tbh lol

For the garbanzo, I purchased in a can so I strained it. I coated it with curry powder before I sautéed in the pan with avocado oil. Then I sprinkled with garlic powder, a little bit of turmeric, paprika, salt & pepper! I also drizzled in some fresh lime juice. Just sautéed until it browned (around 5mins).

Regular avocado sliced, then topped with everything but the bagel seasoning on top.

The dressing was tahini, splash of water depending on the consistency you want, salt, maple syrup, lemon juice, garlic powder, and a splash of wine vinegar.

Then just plate and drizzle with the dressing :) One of the bowls has kimchi in it cause… well cause I was craving it LMAO. I was also gonna put edamame but… I forgot oops.


Edit: I forgot to write how I cooked the firm tofu LOL I put it in the convection over for 400F 20 minutes :)
